items.title: onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent
items.excerpt: Let an AI model use a real iPhone with a $7 ESP32: AirPlay eyes, USB HID hands, any OpenAI-compatible vision model. No Mac, no developer account, no jailbreak.
items.summary: ESP32-based agent control layer enables OpenAI-compatible vision models to operate iPhone hardware via AirPlay streaming and USB HID, requiring only $7 microcontroller, no developer account or jailbreak.
items.usefulness: Could support building agentic systems that learn from real mobile device interaction if vision model integration proves reliable on commodity hardware.
items.to_verify: Whether vision accuracy and latency over AirPlay streaming meets practical thresholds; actual token costs and error rates compared to native APIs.

items.title: Publish fake stats, get cited in LLMs
items.summary: Author documented how fabricated statistics published to web get ingested and cited by LLMs, establishing feedback loop that amplifies false claims through model training data.
items.usefulness: Could inform Python document analysis tools with concrete example of AI governance risk: automated contamination of training corpora through coordinated publication.
items.to_verify: Whether effect persists across different LLM architectures and training dates; how retrieval and ranking systems weighted the fabricated source before being cited.

items.title: StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Decision
items.excerpt: Open decision models from 0.8B to 27B: a calibrated probability for every option in one pass, and a short thought only when unsure. Engine for vLLM, llama.cpp and MLX.
items.summary: Open decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters output calibrated probabilities for options in one forward pass, with short reasoning only when confidence is low; engine support includes vLLM, llama.cpp and MLX.
items.usefulness: If probability calibration claim is validated, could reduce token costs in Python document classification by avoiding unnecessary reasoning steps for high-confidence decisions.
items.to_verify: Actual calibration accuracy metrics against held-out decision tasks; comparison of token usage and latency versus baseline reasoning-always approaches.
